The Free Kick number game (both sides call 1-10, closer call picks ATTACK or DEFEND) is a fairground booth: striped awning with the title on its sign, candy-striped posts, a wheel of fortune that spins and stops under the red flap on the number, raffle tickets for the numbers. old = the dark window with the plain buttons and the line of words at the bottom.
How many numbers the wheel is drawn with. If coin_faces in Tuning.csv is different, the old window is used (the wheel would have the wrong wedges).
The striped roof across the top with the blank yellow sign (pieces drawn by tools/art/clash_wheel_pieces.py).
One candy-striped post; the right one is the same picture flipped. Blank = no posts.

How far down the posts start.
Where the title is written on the sign: left, top, width, height. CALL IT, then THE WHEEL, then who called it or who called closer.
The biggest size of the title; longer titles shrink to fit the sign.
The title's colour (red). The outline is the ink colour.
The ink colour: outlines, and the writing on light tickets.
The writing on dark tickets and the two headings.
The painted wedges, number 1 at the top. This picture turns.
The brown rim with the light bulbs. It stays still.
The gold Groschen in the middle.
The red flap at the top. The wheel stops with the number under its tip.

The radius of the painted face in its picture (do not change unless the picture is redrawn).
How far out the numbers sit on their wedges (share of the radius).
The size of the numbers on the wheel.
The wedge colours in the order the picture repeats them, so each number gets the right ink: dark wedges get cream numbers, light ones ink.
How many whole turns the wheel makes before it stops (plus the way to the number). The time is coin_spin_seconds in Tuning.csv.
Where THEIR CALL is written (middle).
Where YOUR CALL is written (middle).
